clue.text: One struck by particular moment late in game

parts.note: a match is the thing you strike to get a flame
a point is a particular, a single detail, as in 'point by point'

explanation.surface: A player is hit by a ball just as the game reaches its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One struck' reads as a person hit; it is the thing you strike to get a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the stage in tennis when the leading player needs just one more point to win, so it only arrives near the end.

clue.text: Endlessly call him a vile, terribly conniving person

indicators.note: without an end, so the word loses its final letter
the letters are treated terribly, knocked out of order

parts.note: the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone vents about a scheming man by calling him vile names.
explanation.walkthrough: Niccolò Machiavelli wrote The Prince, and his name became a byword for cunning, so a capital-M answer can stand for any schemer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of The Prince advised rulers to use deceit, and his name is now used of any unscrupulous plotter.

clue.text: Channel without lead feature

indicators.note: a word's lead is its front letter, and 'without' says to go on without it

parts.note: a strait is a narrow sea channel
the S at the front is dropped

explanation.surface: A TV channel is missing its main programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television; here it is water, as in the Strait of Dover.

clue.text: How a magician may reveal ropes they rearranged

indicators.note: the letters of 'ropes they' are literally arranged again in a new order

explanation.surface: A conjuror's rope trick: the ropes were tangled and now come out restored.
explanation.walkthrough: The ropes fit the magic show perfectly, which hides that they are only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the exclamation a conjuror makes as the trick is unveiled, so it describes the manner of the unveiling.

clue.text: My friend is former head?

parts.note: old = former, as in 'my old school'

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their pal used to be a headteacher.

clue.text: Lack of cutting implements must put out the last of cafeteria diners

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out the last of cafeteria diners' reads as evicting customers. Nosh is informal British for food.

clue.text: Most of group is featured in performances — they're musicians!

indicators.note: most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end after the dash; 'they're musicians' describes the people, so the plural answer fits.

clue.text: I'm a chic star, frightfully alluring

explanation.walkthrough: The boast is the answer in disguise: a chic star would describe themself exactly this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a compelling personal magnetism that draws people in.

clue.text: Looking sulky, having been denied power trip

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short pleasure excursion, a day out.

clue.text: Bad-tempered piano worker maybe holding another instrument up

clue.text: State expanded once stripped of its borders?

clue.text: Height of king embodied in sculpture

clue.text: Round element making up Bridget Riley work?

clue.text: In two minds, primarily after delaying one's transport to Oz?

clue.text: An elegant interior refurbished over several time periods

clue.text: I'm surprised about operation of a restaurant

clue.text: Meaningful reference book?

clue.text: Artist appeared before the crowd, being filmed
